success_patterns: For collection requests described as current, recent, or upcoming, the first page and a conventional bounded page size can be appropriate even when the user does not specify pagination explicitly.
When an endpoint exposes a content-type parameter, include its documented JSON value when needed for the requested structured response.

patch.reasoning: Several trajectories use paginated match-list endpoints, including an unqualified recent/upcoming request, and three trajectories expose a Content-Type parameter whose expected JSON value was omitted. Clarifying these cases complements the existing rules for explicit pagination and output-format parameters.

edits.target: When the user explicitly requests the first page, pass `page=1` on every applicable paginated call; do the same where applicable when a requested count is served by a paginated endpoint.
edits.content: For an unqualified current, recent, or upcoming collection request, use `page=1` when the endpoint exposes pagination and choose its documented default or smallest conventional page size; avoid unbounded collection requests.

edits.target: Distinguish fields for different levels of a location hierarchy.
edits.content: When an endpoint exposes a documented content-type or response-format parameter, include its value when needed to select the requested structured representation (for example, `application/json`); do not invent unrelated headers or values.
